Release order is this sequence, never a numeric comparison of versions. tools/release_sequence.py reads this file; segments are walked in order and a version's position is (segment index, index within the segment).

segments.name: prehistory
segments.rule: retrospective annotated tags on milestones of the development history (DEVHIST.md, 2026-09-28), not releases: they sort before the first release, are never cut, and gate 01 and the changelog ignore them

segments.name: the 6.7.x series
segments.rule: 6.7.N is followed by 6.7.N+1, or by the first entry of the next segment (6.6.0, the landing sequence); the series has at least one release, 6.7.0 (ember's "6.7")

segments.name: the 6.6 series (the landing sequence)
segments.rule: the landing sequence: it comes chronologically AFTER the 6.7.x series and before 6.6.6 (ember, EMBER.md 2026-10-14 ~15:20 EDT)

segments.name: the final release and after
segments.rule: 6.6.6 is the final release; every release after it appends .6 to the one before (6.6.6.6, 6.6.6.6.6, ...)
